facts: Statistical language modeling remains a challenging task, in particular for morphologically rich languages.
New approaches based on factored language models have been developed to address the problem of statistical language modeling.
Factored language models provide principled ways of including additional conditioning variables other than the preceding words.
Morphological features are additional conditioning variables other than the preceding words.
Syntactic features are additional conditioning variables other than the preceding words.
The number of possible choices for model parameters creates a large space of models.
A large space of models can not be searched exhaustively.
The paper presents an entirely data-driven model selection procedure.
An entirely data-driven model selection procedure is based on genetic search.
An entirely data-driven model selection procedure is shown to outperform knowledge-based selection procedures.
An entirely data-driven model selection procedure is shown to outperform random selection procedures.
An entirely data-driven model selection procedure is shown to outperform on two different language modeling tasks.
The two different language modeling tasks are Arabic and Turkish.
New approaches based on factored language models have been developed recently.
Factored language models provide principled ways of including morphological features as additional conditioning variables.
